notes: Changed rule, graded against the current text: Chain fallible steps with `with`. Since db91c23 it adds "This holds in a public function whose only fallible call is the first step and whose body builds the result: the `with` saves the error clause and costs the reader a search for steps that are not there." and its first example is now a public build/1 with a one-step with (idiomatic-elixir/SKILL.md, under the rule heading). The verdicts still rest on "A `with` has at least two `<-` steps; one step is a `case`." Violating runs out of 5: one-step sentence 0 (no run writes a one-step with, public or private); nested-case clause 0; else sentence (unchanged) 0. In the previous sweep 1 of 5 (sonnet-1, a private one-step with at its line 222) violated.

Three calls decided the with counts, made as in the previous sweep. Haiku-1 (lines 150-152) and haiku-2 (lines 153-155) write a two-step with whose body returns parse_limits/1 or parse_config/1, a third fallible call; the second-step sentence speaks only of a one-step with, and nothing is nested or put in an else, so neither is counted. Sonnet-1's init/1 with (lines 122-130) ends in else / {:error, reason} -> {:stop, reason}, which only rewraps the reason in the tuple init/1 must return, so it is not counted. Opus-1 writes no with: read_limits/1 (lines 130-135) is a case on :file.consult/1 that normalizes its error and returns parse_limits(entries) from the :ok clause; a with there would have one step, which the rule says is a case, and the nested-case sentence is about a with body, so it is graded clean.

The other eight rules are unchanged since db91c23 (the new `do:` rule and the reworded captures and assert rules are not on this case's list) and are graded to the previous sweep's standard: an `if` on one boolean condition is clean; haiku-1's `if is_map(users) and Enum.all?(...)` (line 172) is not the guard-only `if not (...)` the baseline opus run was counted for, because Enum.all?/2 cannot go in a guard; key, entry and row_key for ETS keys, and opus-1's result in require_default(result) (line 162) for a pass-through {:ok, _} | {:error, _}, are not counted, as the previous sweep did not count result or key; caller examples in the moduledoc and example modules without @spec are not counted.

All five runs read the limits file inside init/1: opus-1 line 91 (:file.consult/1 at line 131), haiku-1 line 108 (File.read/1 at line 157), haiku-2 line 110 (line 160), sonnet-1 lines 122-123 (Code.eval_file/1 at line 156), sonnet-2 line 122 (:file.consult/1 at line 168). Opus-1's @doc (lines 39-40) and haiku-2's moduledoc (line 23) say a bad file should make starting fail. The responsive rule names only HTTP calls and large queries as slow work, so, as in the previous two sweeps, no verdict rests on it, but every run misses the case's init check. All five start_link/1 functions accept :name and document it in the start_link @doc (opus-1 line 49, haiku-1 line 74, haiku-2 line 77, sonnet-1 line 81, sonnet-2 line 77), so the previous sweep's Group related parameters entry for options documented in @moduledoc does not recur.

All five runs keep one ETS row per admitted request in a public ordered_set table owned by the GenServer and let the caller insert, count with :ets.select_count/2 and delete its own row when over the limit, with a sweep from handle_info/2, so Pick the abstraction, Use ETS, Keep each process behind one module and the responsive rule are clean in all five, as in the previous sweep. Opus-1, haiku-1 and haiku-2 keep the limits in :persistent_term; sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 keep them as {{:limit, user_id}, limit} rows in the same table, which the sweep's match spec leaves alone. Every run is clean on all nine graded rules, where the previous sweep had sonnet-1 violating the with rule and Naming (it now names its lookup config_path/1).

Each file was formatted, compiled and run in a scratch copy under grading/rate-limiter-skill. All five pass mix format --check-formatted. Haiku-1, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 compile with elixirc --warnings-as-errors. Haiku-2 warns that Jason.decode/1 is undefined because Jason is not installed (with a stub over JSON.decode/1 it compiles with no warnings). Opus-1's full file fails at use MyAppWeb, :controller (line 170) because its example controller and Oban worker need Phoenix and Oban; lines 1-163 compile alone with --warnings-as-errors. In every run a 50-task burst admitted exactly 2 at the default limit of 2 and 5 for a user configured at 5, a second instance under name: :other kept its own count, and a sweep removed one expired row and kept the rest. Haiku-1 and haiku-2 compare user IDs by to_string/1, so 42 and "42" share a count; opus-1, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 key by the raw ID, opus-1 saying so in its moduledoc. Sonnet-1 evaluates the limits file with Code.eval_file/1 (line 156), described as a trusted Elixir script, though its moduledoc example names it priv/rate_limits.terms (line 24); its retry_after/3 now uses :ets.select/3 with a limit and handles :"$end_of_table" (lines 177-183), so the previous sweep's Enum.EmptyError cannot occur. Sonnet-2 takes the default limit from a start option, not the file.

All five runs have rc 0 and a model_id matching their tier. Reads: opus-1 SKILL.md, processes.md, ecto-phoenix.md and library-design.md (the references with one cat command); haiku-1, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 SKILL.md, processes.md and ecto-phoenix.md; haiku-2 SKILL.md and processes.md. Expected reads (processes.md) is met in all five.
